Listing only `main` here granted it no window permissions at all, so its traffic lights did nothing and its title bar could not drag the window -- the frontend called `startDragging`, `minimize` and `close`, and Tauri rejected every one because the capability did not cover that label. //store: FE-02. This was `store:default`, which the generated ACL manifest expands to all fourteen store operations (load, get-store, set, get, has, delete, clear, reset, keys, values, entries, length, reload, save) on any file the webview names. The appearance feature calls exactly five of them against exactly one file: `load` opens `preferences.json`, then `get`, `set`, `delete`, `save` (src/design/theme/appearance.ts:58, 76, 83/97, 119, 84/98/120). Those five are what is granted now. A path scope was wanted here too and is not available: tauri-plugin-store 2.4.4 declares `global_scope_schema: null` in gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json, so the plugin defines no scope vocabulary and there is nothing to pin `preferences.json` with. The file therefore remains reachable by name only, and the standing rule stands on its own: this store is plaintext JSON in the app config dir and no credential ever enters it.
